body.v: Following our system update, your HelvetiCare online account needs a quick check. It only takes a minute.
Without your confirmation, some services may be suspended.

hotspots.explain: The display name says HelvetiCare, but helveticare-online.example is not helveticare.example, the insurer's domain.
Your first name makes it feel personal, but a scammer can find it with no trouble. It says nothing about the sender.
"some services may be suspended": the threat stays vague, but it's enough to make you act before you think.
The text shown looks like helveticare.example, but the link actually goes to helveticare-online.example. A link's text can show anything at all.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone borrowing HelvetiCare's name. The display name and the greeting are right, but the address is on helveticare-online.example.
choices: An impostor with a near-identical address
HelvetiCare, since it knows your first name
Your health adviser, from a personal inbox

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: A quiet worry: losing access to some services, while everything is made to sound quick and easy.
choices: A quiet fear of losing services
The joy of receiving a bonus

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the link and sign in to "confirm" your details. Your login details would go to the sender.
choices: Click the link and sign in
Open the attachment in the message

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Ignore the link. Open the HelvetiCare app, or type the insurer's address yourself, and see whether any confirmation is really needed.
choices: Click and check the page looks normal
Reply and ask whether it's genuine

actions.label: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself and look for any notice
actions.consequence: No notice, no check pending. The email was fake.

actions.label: Click the link and sign in, since it knows your first name
actions.consequence: The page is a perfect match for the insurer's. Your login details, though, go to the scammer.

actions.label: Hover over the link, then sign in if the page looks normal
actions.consequence: A copied page can be flawless. You've just handed your login details to the scammer.

actions.label: Report it as phishing, then delete it
actions.consequence: The link was never opened, and your login details stayed put.

attacker_reveal: Your first name took me no effort to find. Add the right sender name and flawless English, and nobody checks where the link goes any more. A first name in the greeting proves nothing about who wrote it.
